plan: In a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), the dominant strategy is to bid exactly your true value. This is because your payment doesn't depend on your own bid amount (only on the second-highest bid), so bidding higher than value risks negative profit if you win at a price above value, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Bidding truthfully at $24 ensures I win only when profitable and maximizes expected profit given the uniform distribution of competitors' values.

This is a second-price auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In this format, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: if I win, I pay less than my value (profit ≥ 0); if I bid higher than my value, I risk winning at a price above my value (negative profit); if I bid lower, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. With no prior round history to adjust for, my value is $16, so I'll bid exactly that.

This is a second-price auction (I win if highest, but pay the second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding my true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids. If I bid above value, I risk winning at a price exceeding my value (negative profit). If I bid below value, I risk losing auctions I could have profitably won. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value of $24.
